title: Guarded response templates — personal PRD sketch
body:
One-line summary:
A lightweight UX + runtime for teams to author reusable response templates (snippets + slots) that are automatically validated by configurable safety and privacy guardrails before being applied at inference-time. Aim: let product teams pick consistent, high-signal outputs while preventing PII leakage, hallucination patterns, or policy violations.

Context / why now:
- Customers building assistants ask for "stable phrasing" and predictable tone across responses (legal, sales, help docs).
- We currently have ad-hoc prompt libraries; shipping templating in the response path would reduce prompt variance and make rollouts easier.
- Private deployments + Dedicated customers want local control of templates and safety rules.
- Ties into Optimize: templates can be evaluated against eval suites and quality/regression alerts.

Core goals (MVP):
1) Provide a minimal authoring surface: template text with placeholders ({{customer_name}}, {{issue_summary}}), optional markdown/blocks.
2) Runtime enforcement: templates pass a safety check step before being used (PII detection, banned-phrases list, length budget).
3) Per-route template binding + versioning so rollbacks/rollouts are simple.
4) Telemetry: per-template usage, fail/reject rates, quality deltas (via micro-evals).

Success metrics (initial):
- 20% reduction in manual prompt fixes from SE runs in pilot accounts within 2 months.
- Template rejection rate < 5% after editor suggestions (post-tuning).
- 50% of pilot flows using templates for at least 75% of responses.

User stories (prioritized):
- As a product PM, I can author a template and preview with synthetic slot values to see the generated output (quick check).
- As an engineer, I can attach a template to an API route or conversation flow and pin a version.
- As a compliance officer, I can add a banned-phrases list and see why a template was rejected (audit log).
- As an SRE, I want template application to be a lightweight pre-step (reject fast) so we don't add tail latency to response path.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Editor: create/edit templates, preview with sample slots, save version.
- Runtime: apply template substitution -> run safety validators -> if pass, call model with templated prompt; if fail, fallback to original prompt or safe fallback variant.
- Telemetry surfaced in Console: per-template counts, rejections, full-text diff for rejected templates, and per-route success rates.

Design notes / UX ideas:
- Editor has two panes: template editor + preview with toggle between sample/global/context slots.
- Provide a small rule console: show which validators ran (PII, banned-phrases, token-budget). Hover to get explanation + remediation hints.
- Quick-fix suggestions: for banned words, suggest synonyms or remove. For length issues, propose truncation heuristics or compress context.
- Inline annotations when template contains potential privacy risk ("contains email-like pattern").

Runtime flow (very rough):
1) Request arrives -> route matched -> template id resolved (if bound).
2) Server-side template substitution using context slots (synchronous; fall back to client-provided representation if slot missing).
3) Pass substituted text to validators (fast rule checks; optional light classification model for hallucination-risk).
4a) If validators PASS -> send to model with template as part of system/instruction and normal context.
4b) If FAIL -> depending on policy: 1) attempt auto-fix + re-run validation, 2) use a pre-approved safe-fallback template, or 3) return structured error to caller (metrics).

Open performance constraints / considerations:
- Validation must be < 3ms P95 ideally (purely heuristics). If classification model used, push to async or use a very small classifier quantized per deployment.
- Keep substitution deterministic and idempotent; avoid adding extra KV cache churn. Templates should not blow up KV cache keys.

Rollout plan / pilot ideas:
- Pilot with 2 customers: a helpdesk SaaS (customer-facing canned replies) and an internal comms team (consistent legal phrasing).
- Start in Hosted API as opt-in route flag; after stabilization, surface in Dedicated + Private as a toggle in console and policy pack for per-org banned-phrases + safe-fallback rules.
- Phases: alpha (editor + local validation, risk logging only), beta (enforced in non-critical routes), GA (enforced for all bound routes).

Experiment matrix (quick):
- Editor guidance: none / inline suggestions / strict blocking. Measure rejection rate and time-to-author.
- Validator strictness: permissive / balanced / strict. Measure false positives and downstream support tickets.
- Fallback policy: fallback-template / auto-fix / error -> measure user-visible failures and latency impact.

Security & compliance notes:
- Templates are org-scoped; allow admin-level export/import but encrypted at rest for Private deployments.
- Audit log for every template use and rejection. Store only template id + hash in long-term logs, redact slot values unless explicit consent/needs.

Risks & unknowns (brain-dump):
- Templates might encourage over-reliance leading to brittle answers (model might hallucinate outside the template frame).
- Combined with function/tool-calling, ensure templates don't accidentally inject structured payloads that bypass validators.
- Slot injection risk: slots themselves can contain unsafe content; validators must run after substitution.

Short TODOs / follow-ups (me):
- Talk to Ev (Evan) about classifier feasibility for hallucination-risk in <5ms.
- Sketch a Console mock (two-pane) and drop into Product review next Tue.
- Pull sample banned-phrases from Legal & run against 50 existing templates we have in prompt-library to estimate reject rates.
- Check storage model with infra: can template metadata live in small DB shard per-org? Impact on routing?

Notes-to-self / rough snippets:
- Template example:
  Title: "Support escalation reply v1"
  Body: "Hi {{customer_name}}, thanks for the report. Based on the logs you provided, the most likely cause is {{root_cause}}. We've opened ticket {{ticket_id}} and will update you within 24 hours. If you can share {{missing_field}} that would help speed resolution. -- Engineering Team"

- Validator pseudo-rules: detect email/phone patterns, detect sequences like SSN, match banned phrases regex list, ensure token length <= route budget, ensure call-to-action not false-commit ("we will fix by X" unless SLA verified).

Quick rough estimate (engineering ask):
- Editor + API binding ~3 sprints (2 engineers frontend, 1 backend + 1 infra support)
- Runtime validators + small infra ~2 sprints
- Pilot instrumentation + console metrics ~1 sprint

Questions for review meeting:
- Which team takes ownership of rule definitions (Legal vs Customer Success vs Product)?
- Should templates be editable in Dedicated/Private by default or locked until org admin enables?
- Do we want eval hooks by default so Optimize can surface regressions (Y/N)?

-- end of scratch; keep messy. Will clean after convo with Maya and Ev.
